CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep Liu He at the Washington table this week and treat the March 1 List-3 hike as the immediate risk to defuse, not a cue to escalate. Put a concrete purchase package (soy, energy, aircraft) and the already-teed IP/market-access steps on paper, and accept a short extension if a Trump–Xi text is close. Do not raise new tariffs, do not fold Meng/Huawei into the trade track as a new hostage bargain, and do not accept a unilateral U.S. snap-back/enforcement mechanism that would let Washington police our industrial policy.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not existential. Combined Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B of our exports (Lists 1–2 at 25%, List 3 at 10% since 24 Sep 2018), and the Dec 1 G20 truce only suspended the scheduled jump of List 3 to 25% — that hike is still the default if talks fail. Huawei is under a second, sharper track: Meng’s 1 Dec arrest, the 10 Dec Canadian detentions, and the 28 Jan DOJ fraud/sanctions indictment plus formal extradition request. The real economy is already feeling it: seasonally adjusted merchandise exports fell about 8.7% over the lookback (to $197.6B in Feb), U.S. customs imports from China dropped from $49.9B in Sep to $33.0B in Feb, 2018 GDP printed a three-decade low (6.6%; Q4 6.4%), December exports contracted 4.4% y/y, and manufacturing PMI sat below 50. That maps near the +0.5 CHN anchor (export-sector hit + firm-level targeting) but not +1.0: industrial production is still ~5.3% y/y, FX reserves are stable near $3.11T, and CNY strengthened from the Oct ~6.97 peak to ~6.76 by mid-Feb — no financial-stability break. Action should stay mild because the channel that can stop the 25% hike is open: 14–15 Feb talks reported purchase progress with enforcement still disputed; Xi told Lighthizer/Mnuchin the two economies are “inseparable”; Trump on 20 Feb said March 1 is “not a magical date” and floated an extension if a deal is close. Escalation now would likely lock in the hike and deepen the export/Huawei squeeze. Full concession or a large purchase-only giveaway is premature: Trump has already said he may keep tariffs even with a deal, and Lighthizer’s “enforcement, enforcement, enforcement” demand (U.S. verification/snap-back) is a sovereignty cost we should not pre-pay without reciprocal, scheduled tariff relief. Negotiate — buy time, sell purchases, hold the structural line.
key_factors: List 3 still at 10% with a March 1 default hike to 25% on ~$200B unless a deal or extension lands
Live high-level talks (Jan 30 Beijing; Feb 14–15 with Xi; Liu He in Washington this week) with progress on purchases and a deadlock on enforcement/IP/subsidies
Huawei/Meng legal track is a separate high-cost threat that should stay compartmentalized from tariff bargaining
Export contraction and 2018 growth at a three-decade low, but reserves stable and CNY stronger — pressure without collapse
Trump publicly softening the hard deadline while signaling he may keep some tariffs even after a deal

sources_cited.excerpt: List 3 takes effect at 10%. China imposes retaliatory tariffs (5–10%) on ~$60B of US goods. Combined US Section 301 coverage now ~$250B of Chinese imports.
G20 Buenos Aires dinner: Trump and Xi agree to a 90-day negotiation window. Planned Jan 1, 2019 hike of List 3 from 10% to 25% is suspended. Same day: Canada arrests Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou.
US DOJ unseals fraud and sanctions-related charges against Huawei and Meng; US formally requests Meng's extradition from Canada.
Another round of talks (through Feb 15). Progress reported on purchases; enforcement mechanism still disputed.
China merchandise exports (SA) latest $197.6B (2019-02) vs $216.3B (2018-09); change -8.7% over the window.
U.S. imports from China fell from $49.9B (2018-09) to $33.0B (2019-02), -33.9%.
China total reserves ex-gold stable at ~$3.109T (2019-02), essentially unchanged over the window.
CNY/USD strengthened from the late-Oct peak near 6.97 to 6.756 on 2019-02-19 — no acute FX crisis.
Trump said March 1 'is not a magical date' and framed the real question as whether the U.S. will raise tariffs; Liu He–Lighthizer/Mnuchin talks continuing in Washington.
Xi met Lighthizer and Mnuchin; both sides claimed important progress; Trump floated extending the March 1 deadline if a deal is close; enforcement still the remaining thorn.
2018 growth 6.6% and Q4 6.4% — slowest in decades; December exports contracted as tariffs began to bite; Beijing under pressure to stimulate and settle the tariff war.
Lighthizer: an agreement is worth nothing without enforcement; White House still calling the 90-day process a hard deadline unless a satisfactory outcome is reached.
